questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I am studying psychology and wanted to go on exchange in Italy - Milan was the only option in Italy, otherwise I would have had to arrange the exchange by myself. Therefore I chose Milan.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy. The University is very good at sending the information that you need. Information about courses was a bit more difficult. The information needed to find courses and apply and so on was very good, but it wasn't until a week or so before the semester started, that we got information on what courses was actually created and the schedule, but this was not a problem, just a bit of a wait.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Good information on email and good answers to any questions. Not at specific event or anything where you got to meet other exchange students, but this happened along the way either how.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: If you start looking a good time it is not that hard to find a place. I used Airbnb to find an apartment with a friend, and this worked very well. This also ment that we didn't have to pay a big deposit and so on. I know that there are other sites such as spotahome or Italianway that are also good.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Starting to look and book in good time is good - it is expensive to live in Milan, so doing it in good time can be good in terms of maybe saving a bit of money.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Registration went fairly easy, information on how to do it was sent to us. I don't remember it that much, but one or two months before the semester we had to do some registration; checking your email is enough, then you wont miss anything.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Information from the University.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got almost all the classes I wanted. The only reason I didn't was because two of them were scheduled at the same time, but it all settled in the end and probably in a better way than I had originally planned.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just read you email and all will be fine:-)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was not as it is at KU. The courses were easier and with a smaller workload. It was difficult in the way, that it was a different way of learning and not knowing what the level for the exams were, but in general it is easier than at KU. At the University of Milan, the one that KU has an agreement with, they do not have a psychology faculty, so the courses were a part of degrees oriented towards human ressources and social and political science, so in that way the courses are also a bit different than one might be used to, and not oriented that much towards psychology.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching was quite different. It mostly consisted of teacher holding a lecture for one hour and half without a brake, and then that was that. No working in groups or answering question. Also not that many assignments if any.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Employment, inequalities and discrimination in the global labour market + Human ressources management; this was instead of Arbejds- og Organisationspsykologi. 
Research methods in social and political science; this was instead of Avanceret forskningsdesign. 
Conflict management and negotiation; this was an elective course.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
The courses that were instead of the mandatory courses were fine. 
I would recommend the elective course Conflict management and negotiation; the professor were a psychologist, and the course were the best one of the ones I had - more participatory lectures.

questions.answer: Not really any.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: It was much as expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't use any of the non-academic opportunities, so I don't really know about the opportunities.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I didn't really use them, so I am not sure, but I know that ESN also hosted a lot of activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Going out to experience the city:-)

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Going on trips to other parts of Italy. Trains are very good and also Flixbus is a good and cheap solution.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I think the best tip would be to try and talk to them in class. I didn't really get to talk to any. I think this was partly because the lectures wasn't very interactive and the local students already knew each other, so people mostly stuck to themselves and were quick in and out of class.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There were differences, but I didn't really find them challenging, just different :-)

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The more slow tempo and spontaneity. Also the culture of going out more during the week, eating out and so on.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Try to do practical things in good time, go out and explore the city and other parts of the country, if you want to meet other nationalities - try to make an effort to speak to others in class or use the activities hosted by ESN. There are usually a lot of Danes on exchange in Milan, so trying to meet others takes some effort, but being with other Danes is also really nice and it can entail friendships that you can bring home.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not really.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Seeing different parts of Italy and experiencing the culture and differences in this across the country. Meeting new people! Learning about a different education system and learning styles.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: It wasn't as such a challenge, but the teaching was different.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
